2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the plaintiffs filed the suit against the Government for declaration of their title to the suit land. The plaintiff’s case is that the suit land along with other land originally belonged to Kasirun Nessa Chowdhury, wife of Sohrab Ali Chowdhury. After death of Kasirun Nessa Chowdhury and her husband, the suit land devolved on their son Mumik Hosan Chowdhury, defendant No. 2 and daughter Hamida Khatun Chowdhury, defendant No. 6, by way of inheritance. By amicable settlement, the suit land fell in the saham of Hamida Khatun Chowdhury. While possessing the suit land, she submitted her return as per provision of P.O. (President's Order) 98 of 1972. Hamida Khatun Chowdhury being issueless used to cultivate her land by bargadar. A portion of the suit land was being possessed by Niltak Barman by way of licence from her. On 02.10.1979, Enam Ali disclosed to Hamida Khatun that his two sons got lease of the suit land from the Government and as such, he would not pay the share of Barga and after the enquiry by her servant, she came to know that in her return she wrongly stated 3.06 acres of land in Plot No. 544 instead of the suit plot. Hamida Khatun filed a petition to the Revenue Officer for amendment and on 16.10.1979, Miscellaneous Case No.  XIII of 1979-80 was started and the notices were served upon the concerned parties. On 28.04.1980, the Revenue Officer, on receipt of the report of enquiry, amended the return inserting Plot No. 561 in place of Plot No. 544. After that, possession was taken over from leases by beating drum. While in possession of the suit land, Hamida Khatun sold the same to plaintiff Nos. 1-5 by registered deed of sale dated 13.04.1981. While plaintiff Nos. 1-5 have been possessing of the suit land, the brother of Hamida Khatun submitted return in the name Monalik Chowdhury, showing Plot No.  561 instead of Plot No. 544. In that return, the suit plot was wrongly written. Against the order of Revenue Officer, defendants filed an appeal to A.D.C (Additional Deputy Commissioner) (Revenue), who allowed the appeal setting aside the order of Revenue Officer. Subsequently, the plaintiffs filed an appeal against the order of A.D.C (Revenue) before the Land Appeal Board, which upheld the order of the A.D.C. (Revenue). Thus the Government leased out the suit land to the leases and as a result, the plaintiffs' title has been clouded. Hence, the instant suit has been filed. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Hamida Khatun Chowdhury and Momlik Hosan Chowdhury. Subsequently, by amicable settlement, the land in Plot No. 544 fell in the saham of Hamida Khatun Chowdhury and the land in Plot No. 561 fell in the saham of Momlik Hosan Chowdhury. According to P.O. No. 98 of 1972 Momlik Chowdhury submitted return the suit plot No. 561 and the excess land was surrendered in favour of Government and since then the suit land became the property of Government as khash land and the Government leased out the land on yearly basis to Emdadul Huq and Nazubul Islam. While they had been in possession of suit land, Hamida Begum filed a petition for amendment of the return and the Revenue Officer ordered amendment. Against that order, defendants filed an appeal to A.D.C. (Revenue), which was allowed. Against the aforesaid order, Hamida Khatun preferred an appeal before the band Appeal Board, which upheld the order of A.D.C. (Revenue) Hamida Khatun Chowdhury did not have right to transfer the suit land to plaintiff Nos. 1-5 and the document, if any, is produced that would be fraudulent and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Defendant Nos. 3-4 contested the suit by filing a separate written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case is that accepting the statement of surrender, defendant No. 1 on 10.07.1978 leased out 2.90 acres of land to them for the first time for a period of five years and that they had been in possession of the said 2.90 acres of land.
